steps.title: Read data with SELECT
steps.content: SELECT specifies the columns to return. FROM specifies the table. SQL reads the requested rows and columns; it does not change the stored table.
steps.example: SELECT name, marks FROM Student; returns only name and marks for every student.
steps.tip: Use explicit column names in production queries instead of SELECT * when you know the required fields.

steps.title: Filter rows
steps.prompt: Which clause filters rows where marks are at least 70?
steps.explanation: WHERE filters individual rows before grouping or final ordering.

steps.title: Sort and limit results
steps.content: ORDER BY sorts returned rows. ASC is ascending and DESC is descending. In SQL dialects that support it, FETCH FIRST or LIMIT can restrict the number of rows.
steps.example: SELECT name, marks FROM Student ORDER BY marks DESC; puts the highest marks first.

steps.title: Find the top score
steps.prompt: Which query returns students with marks greater than 80, highest marks first?
options: SELECT * FROM Student WHERE marks > 80 ORDER BY marks DESC;
SELECT * FROM Student ORDER BY marks > 80;
SELECT * FROM Student GROUP BY marks > 80;
steps.explanation: WHERE selects rows with marks > 80. ORDER BY marks DESC sorts them from highest to lowest.

steps.title: Aggregate functions
steps.content: COUNT counts rows or non-NULL values; SUM adds values; AVG calculates the mean; MIN and MAX return extremes. GROUP BY creates a separate result group for each key.
steps.example: SELECT department, AVG(salary) FROM Employee GROUP BY department; calculates an average for each department.

questions.prompt: Which clause identifies the source table?
questions.explanation: FROM names the table or tables being queried.

questions.prompt: Which query selects only names from Student?
questions.explanation: SELECT name FROM Student is the correct basic query structure.

questions.prompt: Which clause sorts marks from highest to lowest?

questions.explanation: COUNT(*) counts all rows in the result set.

questions.prompt: Which clause filters groups after aggregation?
questions.explanation: HAVING filters grouped results; WHERE filters rows before grouping.
